--- title: "Cadzow window seams in the CSD" description: "The lfpack Cadzow denoiser left horizontal seams in the CSD at its spatial window boundaries. Two causes, the NP1 checkerboard and the hard adaptive rank, fixed by a full-grid trajectory and Gavish-Donoho shrinkage; bad channels are now estimated by Cadzow. Released in ibl-neuropixel 1.14.0, routed in lfpack." date: "2026-10-09" date-modified: "2026-10-10" author: "Olivier Winter" categories: [electrophysiology, LFP, CSD, Neuropixels, denoising] --- ## Summary **Status: fixed.** The CSD of Cadzow-denoised LFP showed horizontal blocks bounded by the boundaries of Cadzow's spatial windows (every 32 channels). A synthetic field with a known CSD found two causes: 1. **NP1 checkerboard.** Each 20 µm row holds 2 of the 4 lateral positions, so the block-Hankel trajectory of a window is half zeros, which the SVD treats as data. 2. **Hard adaptive rank** (`gap_threshold`). Neighbouring windows keep different numbers of components, so their fits disagree where they are blended. The window gains sum to 1, and the PPCA outlier replacement is not involved. The fix runs Cadzow on the full lateral × depth grid, with the empty positions filled from their neighbours, and replaces the hard rank cut by Gavish–Donoho singular-value shrinkage. On the synthetic field at 3 % noise, the CSD error drops from 0.83 to 0.31 and the seams go away. On the 11 benchmark insertions the window blocks are gone, at the same cost. Bad channels can now be estimated by Cadzow itself, instead of being interpolated before and after it. Near bad channels this brings the CSD error from 0.58 to 0.30, the same as with no bad channels. | PR | Content | Status | |---|---|---| | [ibl-neuropixel#96](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/ibl-neuropixel/pull/96) | `fill_grid`, `shrinkage`; entry points `cadzow_denoiser_np1` / `cadzow_denoiser_np2` with the LFP defaults | merged, released in 1.14.0 | | [ibl-neuropixel#97](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/ibl-neuropixel/pull/97) | `bad_channels`; `cadzow_kwargs["bad_channels_as_missing"]` in the LFP chunk worker | merged, released in 1.14.0 | | [lfpack#22](https://github.com/int-brain-lab/lfpack/pull/22) | Cadzow settings routed by probe geometry (`cadzow_lfp_kwargs`): NP1 → `LFP_KWARGS_NP1`, NP2 → `LFP_KWARGS_NP2` | open, needs the 1.14.0 pin | All the new options are opt-in. With the defaults, `cadzow_denoiser` gives bit-identical output to 1.13.0, and lfpack 1.0.0 passes its tests against 1.14.0. With the new Cadzow, lfpack file sizes are stable per tier, but fidelity to the denoised input drops by about 2 dB; see [lfpack v05](../2026-10-lfpack-v05/index.qmd). ## The problem Cadzow (`ibldsp.cadzow.cadzow_denoiser`, as called by lfpack v04 with `rank=5, fmax=None, nswx=64, ovx=32, gap_threshold=2, ppca_k=2`) fits a rank ≤ 5 model per frequency bin in spatial windows of 64 channels (640 µm), blended every 32 channels. The CSD, a second spatial derivative, shows the disagreement between neighbouring window fits A and B through the w″·(A − B) and 2w′·(A′ − B′) terms of the blend. The blending weights only shape the seams; the disagreement between the fits sets their size. Seams were most visible where Cadzow keeps little CSD power, e.g. in 749cb2b7. ## Diagnosis on a synthetic field The synthetic field has 40 laminar disc sources (R = 500 µm, σ = 1/3 S/m) with log-uniform widths of 50–300 µm and 1/f^1.4 time courses, forward-modelled onto NP1, plus white noise. At 3 % noise, Cadzow keeps the same CSD fraction as on the real chunks. Metrics: - **CSD error:** median per-channel RMS error of the CSD against the true CSD, relative to the true CSD RMS. - **Seam ratio:** error within ±2 channels of the window boundaries over the error elsewhere; 1 means no seams. Without noise, production Cadzow already has a CSD error of 0.54 with seams (ratio 1.89), so the seams are not a noise problem (`cadzow_synthetic_remedies.py`): - **Checkerboard.** On the channel trajectory, a fixed rank 5 still leaves seams (1.90), as it splits component pairs. On the full grid it is near exact (CSD error 0.02, seams 1.16). - **Hard adaptive rank.** On the full grid with the production adaptive rank, the seams are back (2.10). - **No fixed rank works with noise.** At 3 % noise, a fixed rank has no seams but does not denoise (CSD error 1.4 to 2.9). The adaptive rank denoises but makes seams. Shrinkage does both (@tbl-synthetic). ::: {#tbl-synthetic .cell tbl-cap='Synthetic field: CSD error and seam ratio of production Cadzow and of full grid + Gavish-Donoho shrinkage, by white-noise level (fraction of the signal RMS).' execution_count=1} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

Figure of ibl-neuropixel#96.](figures/2026-10-10_cadzow_pr96_fill_grid_shrinkage.webp){#fig-pr96 .lightbox} The shrinkage noise scale is calibrated on white noise, so that the largest noise singular value lands on the Marchenko–Pastur bulk edge. It is 2.25 for NP1 with the full grid and 1.22 for NP2, whose grid is already full. The NP1 value applied to NP2 brings the seams back (@tbl-np2), hence the two entry points. ::: {#tbl-np2 .cell tbl-cap='NP2 (single shank) synthetic field: CSD error and seam ratio with the v04 settings and with shrinkage at the NP2 and NP1 noise scales.' execution_count=2} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

Each was then denoised, and bad channels were re-interpolated as in production. The full-grid shrinkage keeps a little more CSD power (median 0.19 against 0.17 of the no-Cadzow CSD RMS). It runs in 27.0 s against 25.6 s per chunk, single-threaded. An interpolated channel is a weighted mean of its neighbours. It does not follow the per-column curvature that the CSD measures, so each bad channel leaves a line in the CSD. With `bad_channels`, Cadzow discards their data, fills them like the empty grid positions, and outputs its own estimate. On the synthetic field with the bad-channel layout of e8f9fba4, this matches the error of the field without bad channels (@tbl-bad). ::: {#tbl-bad .cell tbl-cap='Synthetic field at 3 % noise with the e8f9fba4 bad channels (11 dead, 7 noisy): CSD error on the channels whose CSD involves a bad channel, and elsewhere.' execution_count=5} ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=5} ```{=html}

`cadzow_denoiser` defaults are unchanged. Its output is bit-identical to 1.13.0 on 4 configurations: the defaults, the v04 settings, `ovx = 48`, and a small window with padding. - The LFP chunk worker re-interpolates bad channels after Cadzow as before, unless `bad_channels_as_missing` is set. - lfpack 1.0.0 passes its 92 tests against 1.14.0. With lfpack#22, `cadzow_kwargs={}` gives the geometry defaults; explicit keys override them. - Multi-shank probes are refused by the routing: their per-shank coordinates repeat across shanks, so `fill_grid` is undefined. The plain path already mixed the shanks on 1.13.0. ## Compression {#compression} The effect on lfpack is in [lfpack v05](../2026-10-lfpack-v05/index.qmd): - **File size:** stable per tier. - **Fidelity:** about 2 dB lower against the denoised input. - **Seams:** the window-dependence check on the real chunks shows no window seams with v05. - **Bad-channel lines:** they halve with the bad channels left to Cadzow. - **CSD:** the codec, not Cadzow, now limits the CSD of the archives. ## Earlier attempts Before the synthetic field, three remedies were tried on the real chunks. They treated the blending, not the fits. - **Two runs staggered by 1/4 and 3/4 of the window step**, blended with complementary raised-cosine weights. This was worse: depth-varying weights add w″ and w′ terms everywhere (`cadzow_stagger.py`). - **Cycle spinning** over 4 grid offsets, averaged with equal weights (`cadzow_cycle_spin.py`). - **More overlap**, `ovx = 48`. Cycle spinning and `ovx = 48` weakened the seams, but kept less CSD power (0.14 against 0.17) and left discontinuities at the same depths in all methods. MSSA (column-stacked Hankel, `cadzow_mssa_real.py`) has no zeros in its trajectory but denoises too little (CSD kept 0.67). ## Code and data | File | Content | |---|---| | `cadzow_window_gain.py` | Window gains sum to 1; trajectory occupancy | | `cadzow_synthetic.py`, `cadzow_synthetic_calibration.py` | Synthetic field, calibration against the real CSD kept | | `cadzow_synthetic_remedies.py`, `cadzow_fill.py` | Fixed ranks, full-grid fill | | `cadzow_shrink.py`, `cadzow_synthetic_shrink.py`, `cadzow_shrink_real.py` | Gavish-Donoho shrinkage prototype, synthetic and real | | `cadzow_synthetic_bad.py`, `cadzow_bad_real.py` | Bad channels as missing grid positions | | `cadzow_synthetic_np2.py` | NP2 geometry | | `cadzow_pr_figures.py` | PR figures, with the ibldsp API | Inputs are the production chunks cached in `~/scratch/lfp/csd_lfpack_v04/` by `../2026-10-csd/plot_cadzow_csd.py`.
